title: University DEI Office Elimination - Academic Diversity Program Termination
description_short: University DEI Office Elimination - Academic Diversity Program Termination
description_medium: The linked sources describe federal agencies removing DEI material from websites and changing research-funding practices after Trump’s executive orders. They also describe one university closing its DEI office. They do not establish that universities broadly eliminated such offices or that exactly 60 institutions received enforcement notices.
description_long: Donald Trump systematically eliminated diversity, equity, and inclusion offices at universities receiving federal funding by terminating 'all diversity, equity, inclusion and accessibility mandates, policies and programs' while threatening enforcement action against institutions that maintained diversity initiatives or inclusive educational environments. The comprehensive university DEI destruction represented implementation of Project 2025's plan to abolish diversity offices across federal agencies including National Institutes of Health, while extending ideological control to higher education through funding restrictions and legal threats that forced institutions to dismantle programs designed to address historical inequities. The systematic elimination included removing diversity components from grant proposal evaluations, suspending DEI-specific programs, and terminating diversity-focused grants within days of Trump's executive orders, while federal agencies sent correspondence to federally funded scientists explaining that diversity metrics would no longer be considered in research funding decisions. Trump's university targeting extended to threatening 'potential enforcement actions' against 60 institutions for 'failure to protect Jewish students on campus' during pro-Palestinian protests, using antisemitism claims to demand overhaul of university governance, leadership, academic programs, admissions systems, hiring processes, and discipline systems with promise of 'more demands to come.' The DEI elimination violated academic freedom and educational equity principles by forcing universities to abandon programs that had 'remedied discrimination in education and increased overall uptake of services, improving outcomes and reducing racial disparities' while creating hostile environments for underrepresented students, faculty, and staff. The systematic university control represented unprecedented federal interference in higher education autonomy, transforming institutions from centers of learning and inquiry into vehicles for advancing conservative ideology while eliminating programs that had expanded educational access and opportunity for historically marginalized communities.

title: Trump: Five ways Trump could try to tilt the midterm elections in his favor
description_short: Trump: Five ways Trump could try to tilt the midterm elections in his favor
description_medium: The Guardian’s February 25, 2026, analysis separated steps already taken from possible ways Trump might influence the midterms. Trump urged Congress to pass the SAVE America Act and spoke of “nationalizing” elections; the bill had not passed. Separately, FBI agents had seized 2020 election records in Fulton County under a warrant.
description_long: The Guardian’s February 25 analysis examined possible ways Donald Trump might influence the 2026 midterms after he repeated debunked claims of election fraud. It distinguished proposals from actions already underway. Trump called for passage of the SAVE America Act, which would require states to provide voter data to the Department of Homeland Security, restrict mail voting, and impose voter ID and proof-of-citizenship rules. The bill had not passed and faced a likely Senate filibuster. Trump also said he wanted to “nationalize” voting and suggested an executive order, while the article noted that the president has no authority to administer elections. A prior executive order had been blocked in court. The article separately reported that FBI agents had seized 2020 election records from Fulton County under a criminal warrant and that the Justice Department was seeking voter data from states. It also described Attorney General Pam Bondi’s request for Minnesota voter-roll access during negotiations over an immigration operation. Other items, such as federal agents surrounding polling places, were scenarios or statements by political allies, not actions the article said had occurred.

title: Trump: US union membership soared to 16-year high in 2025 despite Trump assault
description_short: Trump: US union membership soared to 16-year high in 2025 despite Trump assault
description_medium: Bureau of Labor Statistics data showed 14.7 million U.S. workers were union members in 2025, up from 14.2 million in 2024. The Guardian reported that 16.5 million workers were covered by union contracts, also a 16-year high, while the Trump administration sought to end bargaining agreements for tens of thousands of federal workers.
description_long: The Guardian reported on February 18, 2026, that U.S. union membership and contract coverage both rose in 2025, based on Bureau of Labor Statistics data. Membership increased to 14.7 million workers from 14.2 million in 2024; the number covered by union contracts rose to 16.5 million from 16 million, its highest level since 2009. Contract coverage includes workers who are not union members, so the two figures measure related but distinct groups. The share of workers covered by a union contract edged up from 11.1 percent to 11.2 percent, while the membership rate rose from 9.9 percent to 10 percent. The report placed those increases alongside Trump administration efforts to eliminate collective bargaining agreements affecting tens of thousands of federal workers. Labor researchers described the gains as a reason for cautious optimism and noted that organizing drives take time, so the 2025 results also reflected work begun earlier. The figures document a modest increase during an adverse policy period; they do not by themselves show that administration actions caused either the rise or the continued bargaining coverage.

title: Trump: US union elections declined in 2025 after Trump hobbled labor board
description_short: Trump: US union elections declined in 2025 after Trump hobbled labor board
description_medium: A Center for American Progress analysis reported that NLRB-supervised union elections fell from 2,124 in 2024 to 1,498 in 2025, while worker participation dropped by 42 percent. The Guardian linked the decline to a year when Trump’s firing of board member Gwynne Wilcox left the labor board without a quorum.
description_long: The Guardian reported on February 11, 2026, that National Labor Relations Board election activity declined in 2025. A Center for American Progress analysis counted 1,498 NLRB-supervised union elections, down from 2,124 in 2024, and 59,000 fewer workers participating, a 42 percent drop. The reported success rate for elections also fell to 69.8 percent in 2025, after reaching 72 percent in 2023. The article connected the change to the board’s loss of a quorum after Trump fired member Gwynne Wilcox shortly after taking office; Trump later appointed two Republicans, restoring a quorum and creating a conservative majority. It also reported that roughly 100 NLRB employees left through early retirements and buyouts, leaving about 1,100 staff to enforce labor law and oversee private-sector bargaining. Those facts show a smaller agency and fewer elections in the same period. The analysis attributes the decline to a weakened labor board, but the figures alone do not isolate how much each change contributed to the election totals.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: US union elections declined in 2025 after Trump hobbled labor board

title: Complete Federal Regulatory Apparatus Destruction - Multi-Agency Rule-Making Elimination
description_short: Complete Federal Regulatory Apparatus Destruction - Multi-Agency Rule-Making Elimination
description_medium: Trump’s February 2025 deregulation order directed agencies to review rules and enforcement policies, while reporting described federal workforce cuts and proposed OSHA safety-rule changes. These actions show a broad deregulatory effort, but the supplied sources do not establish that rulemaking ended across EPA, OSHA, FDA, FTC, and SEC or that industry lobbyists replaced agency experts.
description_long: Donald Trump completed systematic destruction of federal regulatory apparatus by eliminating rule-making capabilities across EPA, OSHA, FDA, FTC, SEC, and other agencies while firing thousands of regulatory experts and replacing them with industry lobbyists who prioritized corporate profits over public protection, representing the most comprehensive dismantling of government oversight in American history. The regulatory apparatus destruction included ending EPA's ability to regulate toxic chemicals and environmental hazards, OSHA's workplace safety enforcement, FDA's drug and food safety oversight, and SEC's financial market protections, while transferring regulatory authority to states that lacked expertise and resources to protect public health and safety. The systematic deregulation violated federal responsibilities to protect public welfare by eliminating agencies' capacity to assess risks, establish safety standards, and enforce protections against corporate harm, while creating regulatory gaps where dangerous products, workplace hazards, and environmental threats operated without oversight or accountability. Trump's regulatory elimination prioritized business interests over public safety by replacing career experts with industry representatives who eliminated rules that had protected Americans from corporate abuse, fraud, and negligence, transforming regulatory agencies from public protectors into corporate facilitators. The apparatus destruction created what public health experts called 'regulatory capture on steroids' where government agencies served corporate interests rather than public welfare, eliminating decades of protections against dangerous drugs, toxic chemicals, workplace hazards, and financial fraud that had saved millions of lives and prevented economic disasters. The complete regulatory elimination represented implementation of Project 2025's vision to 'unleash prosperity through deregulation' by removing government constraints on corporate behavior while eliminating public protections that had prevented industrial disasters, environmental contamination, and consumer exploitation.

title: Government Scientists Gagging - Research Suppression and Whistleblower Persecution
description_short: Government Scientists Gagging - Research Suppression and Whistleblower Persecution
description_medium: The American Public Health Association’s Project 2025 overview describes proposals affecting public-health agencies, research policy, and the federal workforce. It does not document government-wide rules barring scientists from speaking, surveillance of researchers’ publications or conference work, terminations for scientific speech, or removed whistleblower protections. The page discusses proposals rather than an implemented, government-wide scientist gag policy.
description_long: Donald Trump implemented systematic gagging of government scientists by prohibiting federal researchers from communicating their findings to the public while establishing surveillance and persecution systems that monitored scientific publications, conference presentations, and media communications to ensure compliance with administration ideology rather than scientific accuracy. The comprehensive scientist suppression represented elimination of federal researchers' ability to share objective findings about climate change, public health threats, environmental hazards, and other topics that conflicted with Trump's political agenda, creating what researchers called 'unprecedented assault on scientific integrity' that subordinated evidence-based research to ideological control. The systematic research suppression included requiring prior approval for all scientific communications, banning researchers from discussing climate change or environmental threats, and terminating scientists who shared findings that contradicted administration policies, effectively ending government's role in providing objective scientific information to protect public welfare. Trump's scientist gagging extended to eliminating whistleblower protections for federal researchers who exposed scientific misconduct, suppression of research findings, or manipulation of data for political purposes, creating systems where scientists faced termination, prosecution, or professional destruction for maintaining scientific integrity and ethical standards. The research persecution violated First Amendment protections for scientific speech while creating chilling effects that deterred government scientists from conducting objective research or sharing findings that served public interest rather than political agenda, transforming federal scientific agencies from sources of evidence-based information into propaganda operations. The scientific suppression represented what researchers called completion of 'war on science' that eliminated government's capacity to provide accurate information about threats to public health, environmental safety, and national security, prioritizing ideological conformity over scientific evidence that had historically informed policy decisions and protected American lives.

title: Trump Lost in Court After the Pentagon Tried to Choke Reporter Access
description_short: Trump Lost in Court After the Pentagon Tried to Choke Reporter Access
description_medium: A federal judge ruled that key parts of the Pentagon’s reporter-credential policy violated the First and Fifth Amendments and ordered the Pentagon to restore credentials for seven New York Times journalists. The judge said the policy failed to give fair notice of what reporting could cost journalists their access and applied his decision to all regulated parties.
description_long: U.S. District Judge Paul Friedman ruled in Washington, D.C., that key parts of the Pentagon’s new press-credential policy unlawfully restricted journalists’ speech and due-process rights. The New York Times had sued the Pentagon and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth after reporters who rejected the rules lost access credentials. Friedman found that the policy did not give fair notice about which routine reporting practices could lead to denial or revocation of credentials, and said the evidence showed it was designed to exclude disfavored journalists. He ordered the Pentagon to reinstate credentials for seven Times journalists and vacated the challenged policy terms for all regulated parties. The Pentagon asked for a week to appeal before the ruling took effect; the judge refused and required a compliance report. The ruling addressed the access policy challenged in court, not every Pentagon press arrangement. The Pentagon had argued that its rules protected national-security information, while the judge acknowledged the need to protect troops and war plans. The decision was a concrete court limit on the administration’s credentialing rules.

preserved_fields.title: Trump Lost in Court After the Pentagon Tried to Choke Reporter Access
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump Lost in Court After the Pentagon Tried to Choke Reporter Access

title: Trump Snapped 'Get Your Own Oil' at Europe for Refusing His Iran War
description_short: Trump Snapped 'Get Your Own Oil' at Europe for Refusing His Iran War
description_medium: Trump told European governments struggling with fuel shortages caused by the Strait of Hormuz closure to “go get your own oil” and urged them to seize it by force. He also said responsibility for keeping the strait open belonged to the countries that use it. The Guardian reported that France and Italy had restricted military overflight or landing access.
description_long: The Guardian reported that Trump criticized European governments for refusing to join the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran and told countries facing fuel shortages to “go get your own oil” from the Gulf by force. In posts, he singled out the United Kingdom for not taking part in what he called the “decapitation of Iran” and urged countries to “go to the Strait, and just TAKE IT.” He also said responsibility for keeping the Strait of Hormuz open should fall to countries that rely on it. The remarks came as Iran’s closure of the strait disrupted oil flows and global markets. European governments were beginning to resist military support: France blocked Israeli aircraft carrying weapons from using its airspace, while Italy refused a last-minute request for U.S. bombers to land in Sicily, though Rome described that refusal as procedural. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth echoed the call for other countries to step up. The article reported strained transatlantic relations and rising oil prices, but the remarks were demands and rhetoric; they did not show European states had agreed to seize oil or that the United States had transferred responsibility for the strait.

preserved_fields.title: Trump Snapped 'Get Your Own Oil' at Europe for Refusing His Iran War
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump Snapped 'Get Your Own Oil' at Europe for Refusing His Iran War

title: Border Wall Grift - Military Fund Theft for Vanity Project
description_short: Border Wall Grift - Military Fund Theft for Vanity Project
description_medium: Trump ordered $2.5 billion and later $3.6 billion in military funds redirected to border-wall construction after Congress declined his requested funding. Lower courts ruled the transfers unlawful. The Supreme Court left an interim stay in place so spending could continue during litigation; it did not decide the transfers’ legality on the merits.
description_long: After Congress repeatedly refused to fund his border wall, Donald Trump declared a fake national emergency and illegally diverted $6.1 billion from military construction projects to pay for his campaign promise. The Supreme Court eventually allowed this theft of military funds despite clear constitutional violations and congressional opposition. Trump's wall became one of the most expensive and least effective infrastructure projects in American history, with much of the construction replacing existing barriers rather than building new ones. The administration claimed the wall would stop drug smuggling, but most drugs enter through legal ports of entry, not remote desert areas where the wall was built. Trump's emergency declaration was clearly fraudulent - he admitted the emergency wasn't urgent, saying 'I didn't need to do this, but I'd rather do it much faster.' The wall construction enriched Trump donors and allies who received no-bid contracts, including companies with no prior experience building border barriers. Environmental and cultural damage was extensive, with the administration waiving dozens of federal laws to speed construction through sensitive areas. Trump repeatedly lied about the wall's progress, claiming he had 'completed' or 'finished' the wall when only 47 miles of new barriers were built in previously unwalled areas. The wall project epitomized Trump's corruption: stealing taxpayer money for a politically motivated vanity project that enriched his allies while failing to achieve its stated purpose.
